overview: S27 is the explosion packet: it carries the knockback vector the client must apply plus the destroyed block records. Anticheats read the velocity component on the OUT side and require it in the client's subsequent motion, exactly like entity knockback, and the block records give simulation anticheats the world mutation the explosion caused. The corpus shows two approaches: Grim brackets the explosion vector with transactions and flags when the prediction misses it, while NCP and Intave read the vector straight off the wire (NCP feeds it into the moving velocity model, Intave into its motion tracker).

checks.name: ExplosionHandler / AntiExplosion (Grim)
checks.purpose: Requires the client's simulated motion to include the explosion knockback vector, flagging players who ignore it.
checks.how_it_works: On the OUT explosion packet, applies the destroyed block records to the compensated world (with 1.21.2+ handling where blocks arrive via separate block-change packets) and records the knockback vector in a transaction-bracketed queue. On each prediction complete, the offset between the player's actual movement and the required explosion velocity is measured; offsets above the configured threshold flag with a setback, and knockback-overridden explosions are exempted by comparing transaction ordering.
checks.detects: Anti-explosion and velocity-cancel cheats that ignore explosion knockback, and world-desync from missing block destruction.
checks.variations: NCP and Intave read the vector directly; Grim additionally simulates the block destruction, which is unique in the corpus.

checks.name: VelocityAdapter (NoCheatPlus)
checks.purpose: Feeds the explosion knockback vector into NCP's moving velocity model so survivalfly and other movement checks allow it.
checks.how_it_works: ProtocolLib adapter on the OUT explosion packet: reads the three velocity floats (indices 1-3), skips packets with zero velocity, and adds the vector to the player's MovingData with the ORIGIN_EXPLOSION and ADDITIVE flags. The moving checks then know the player was legitimately pushed and subtract the explosion velocity from their expected motion.
checks.detects: Anti-explosion cheats are caught indirectly: without the recorded push, the movement checks treat the explosion's motion as impossible.
checks.variations: Grim requires the exact vector in prediction; NCP adds it to an expected-motion model that moving checks consume.

checks.name: ExplosionReader (Intave)
checks.purpose: Reads and rewrites the explosion knockback vector into the Intave motion abstraction for both simulation and mitigation.
checks.how_it_works: ProtocolLib reader over the OUT explosion packet: on pre-1.21.3 servers it reads velocity floats 1-3, on 1.21.3+ it reads the optional motion vector, converting either into a Motion value; setMotion writes the value back. The motion feeds Intave's fake-player simulation and its mitigation layer, which can resend corrected motion.
checks.detects: Anti-explosion and knockback reduction, detected through the simulation's motion comparison and mitigated by rewriting the sent vector.
checks.variations: NCP reads floats only; Intave supports both wire formats and can write the vector back, which NCP never does.
